examples.solution_text:
Read the endpoints and divide the distance covered by the time taken.

(a) The first stage runs from $(0,0)$ to $(2,14)$.
$\begin{align*}s&=\frac{14-0}{2-0}\\&=7\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$

(b) From $(2,14)$ to $(3,14)$, the distance does not change, so the speed is $0\text{ km/h}$.

(c) The final stage runs from $(3,14)$ to $(5,34)$.
$\begin{align*}d&=34-14\\&=20\text{ km} \end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}t&=5-3\\&=2\text{ h}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}s&=\frac{20}{2}\\&=10\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$
Use the changes in distance and time rather than the final readings.

(a) The return runs from $(1.5,18)$ to $(3,0)$. Use the size of the decrease in distance from home.
$\begin{align*}d&=18-0\\&=18\text{ km}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}t&=3-1.5\\&=1.5\text{ h}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}s_{\text{return}}&=\frac{18}{1.5}\\&=12\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$
Speed is positive even though the line slopes down.

(b) The outward stage runs from $(0,0)$ to $(1,18)$.
$\begin{align*}s_{\text{outward}}&=\frac{18}{1}\\&=18\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$
Since $18>12$, the outward stage was faster.

The final stage runs from $(15,1500)$ to $(30,4500)$. Convert metres to kilometres and minutes to hours.

$\begin{align*}d&=4500-1500\\&=3000\text{ m}\\&=3\text{ km}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}t&=30-15\\&=15\text{ min}\\&=\frac{15}{60}\text{ h}\\&=0.25\text{ h}\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}s&=\frac{3}{0.25}\\&=12\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$

(a) Read each cyclist’s moving segment from the common axes.

A travels from $(0,0)$ to $(3,27)$.
$\begin{align*}s_A&=\frac{27}{3}\\&=9\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$

B travels from $(0,0)$ to $(1.5,21)$, then stops. The horizontal stage is excluded from riding time.
$\begin{align*}s_B&=\frac{21}{1.5}\\&=14\text{ km/h}\end{align*}$

(b) Since $14>9$, B was faster while moving.

coverage.summary: Retained all four examples and covered all six distinct assessed methods without adding examples or changing assessment content. Solutions remain editable prose and inline mathematics and inherit #268cff from TheoryView. Graphs preserve their mathematical data and semantic colours. Assessment mappings classify methods only; accepted practice and quiz mathematics were not re-audited. No files were written.

examples.derivation: The graph gives endpoints (0,0), (2,14), (3,14) and (5,34). First-stage speed is (14−0)/(2−0)=7 km/h. The horizontal stage has zero distance change, giving 0 km/h. Final-stage distance is 34−14=20 km and duration is 5−3=2 h, giving 10 km/h. This follows Bella’s first-leg and second-leg calculations and the horizontal-segment key idea.

The return segment runs from (1.5,18) to (3,0). Distance covered is 18 km in 1.5 h, giving positive speed 12 km/h. Outward travel covers 18 km in 1 h, giving 18 km/h; therefore the outward stage is faster. The graph preserves these endpoints and the intervening stop. Return-speed calculations are supported by Ben’s bushwalk and the worksite journey.

The final segment runs from (15,1500) to (30,4500). Distance covered is 3000 m=3 km. Elapsed time is 15 min=15/60 h=0.25 h. Speed is 3/0.25=12 km/h. The graph scales and plotted points agree. The supplied prior-knowledge conversions and Bella’s elapsed-time method support the combined conversion calculation.

A covers 27 km in 3 h, giving 9 km/h. B covers 21 km in 1.5 h, giving 14 km/h, then remains stationary. Excluding B’s stop is appropriate for speed while moving. Since 14>9, B is faster while moving. Both plotted series and their legend distinctions agree with the working. Shared-axis speed calculations and excluding stops are supported by the motorists and Flo–Chloe exercises.

review.summary: All 22 exact assessment locators are mapped appropriately without repeating their accepted mathematical audit. The four examples cover initial, later and return segments, speed comparisons, unit conversions and selecting moving segments on common axes. All existing examples retain their mathematical content; none requires removal. Separate question and solution fields keep answers hidden, and solution prose/math inherits the supplied blue styling. The aligned calculations need no phantom equals because their opening rows contain explicit equations. Editable diagrams preserve scales, values and semantic colours; solution prose supplies endpoint annotations. No syllabus exception is required. Final printed typography and layout remain subject to the later capture stage. No files were written.
